suppress.notes:
Suppress all for this javax.servlet api package: There are lots of false positives, simply because its version number is way beyond the remaining org.eclipse.jetty jar files. Note, that our actual Jetty version is different.
As long as we don't suppress anything in org.eclipse.jetty:jetty-server or :jetty-servlet, vulnerabilities will still trigger if we actually use an outdated Jetty version.
Suppress false positive, because com.google.common.io.Files.getTempDir() is not used

Jetty 10 is EOL, so its vulnerabilities will never be fixed upstream. Suppress the NVD findings, which are matched via the CPE identifiers of the jars (vendor is reported as eclipse, jetty and mortbay_jetty alike).
Scoped to the 10.x line on purpose: as soon as we move to Jetty 11/12, this rule stops applying and vulnerabilities are reported again.

Same as above, but for findings that are not matched via a CPE: OSS Index reports vulnerabilities against the package URL directly, so they survive any <cpe> suppression and have to be matched by name.
